name: Oriental Fuchsia
lede: Oriental Fuchsia is a dark, saturated reddish purple named for the fuchsia flower, and like its close neighbor [[orchid-purple|Orchid purple]], it does not appear in our painting archive at all.

sections.title: A flower's name, darkened
sections.body:
The library records Oriental Fuchsia from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 53 E 12, first recorded in 1925 [1]. The ISCC-NBS lists classify its computed category as a deep reddish purple, far darker than the fuchsia flower's own bright pink-magenta [1]. "Oriental" here is a period marketing word rather than a documented link to any place; the books we checked do not explain it [1].

The nearest named color in the library is [[byzantium|Byzantium]], about 3.2 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[grape|Grape]] and [[bruise|Bruise]] close behind it [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 32, chroma 43, hue 340 degrees, Munsell 2.5RP 3.2/8.9 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Oriental Fuchsia is not a painter's color [2]. No painting in our archive of 23,781, as photographed, has a color within a small distance of this swatch covering even five percent of the canvas [2]. That describes our own archive, not painting as a whole; a color this dark and this saturated in red-violet is rare among natural pigments [2].
